lastCompletedStory.title: WARNING: install.sh's success path has zero execution coverage

nextStoryContext: Added the missing success-leg test for install.sh (`describe('install.sh success path (US-R2-004, CAM-460)')`). The existing `writeFakeCurl` PATH-shim helper (US-R1-001) gained a third `'success'` behavior variant that inspects its own argv for a `-o <path>` flag: when present it writes dummy bytes to that path (standing in for the asset download at line `curl -fsSL "${URL}" -o "${TMP_BIN}"`) and exits 0; when absent it falls through to the releases-list JSON response used by the pre-existing error-path tests. One shim now answers both of install.sh's two distinct curl call shapes (stdout-piped JSON list vs. positional-URL + `-o` download), so no second shim file was needed. The new test asserts real filesystem side effects, not just existence: both `gateship` and `gship` land in `GATESHIP_INSTALL_DIR` with the executable bit set (`statSync(dest).mode & 0o111 > 0`), and a pre-seeded `cam` file in the same install dir survives byte-for-byte (`readFileSync` equality before/after), proving the install loop's additive-over-`cam` claim (ADR-0055) is actually exercised, not just grepped. Full `bun run check:all` is green: 5993 pass / 0 fail, typecheck clean, lint/file-size/debt-markers/coverage/dead-code/dup/ci-parity/agents-md/test-sleeps/skip-ratchet all ok; no vendor/templates files touched. Appended a bullet to patterns.md documenting the single-shim-branches-on-argv-shape pattern for testing download scripts.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Test-only change extending an existing bash PATH-shim test helper (bun:test); no new external library surface exercised.
